<!--
WHAT THIS IS. Figure 3 was assembled by merging three older figures, one about the residual, one
about the score and one about the score variance, and taking the discriminating row from each. This
carries what the merge left out, over all seven members (LSE / NR / INR / R / MR / VR / IR):
  A  the residual property the parent does not draw: the MEAN standardized residual.
  B  the score bias for the parameters the parent does not draw: k_on, the unitary current, and the
     instrumental noise level.
  C  the score autocorrelation for those same three.
The parent draws the second residual moment (its row B), the score bias and the autocorrelation for
k_off and N_ch (rows D and G), and, since 2026-07-31, the residual autocorrelation beside the score
in row G. Between the two figures every check is drawn once and none twice.

WHY IT IS A SUPPLEMENT AND NOT A CUT. Two of the three rows are near-null and that is the point: a
referee asking "did you check the first moment, and did you check the parameters you do not show"
gets an answer that cost no body space. Job D in the guide, the standard check the field expects.
Row A also completes the trio 03_diagnostics.tex enumerates for r_t -- mean zero, unit variance, no
autocorrelation -- whose other two members are in the parent.

WHAT ROW A IS WORTH, measured before it was drawn: the mean standardized residual over the whole
record is 0.0149, 0.0103, 0.0093, 0.0051, 0.0040, 0.0038 and 0.0037 down the ladder. Nothing
separates. That is the
row's claim, and it is also why the row is here and not in the body: a non-difference is stated
better by four numbers in a caption than by a row of panels, which is the rule that removed the grey
reference from supplement 1 on the same day. Completeness is what a supplement is for, and this
earns exactly that much.

WHY THE NOISE LEVEL IS ON ROW B, and it is not filler. It is the CONTROL direction. Figure 4 reports
that the information distortion departs from one in neither recursive member along the instrumental
noise, the one direction where the shrinkage rule paints nothing, so an unbiased score there is the
negative control for the directions that are biased. It also behaves unlike every other parameter in
time: the noise level is measured BEFORE the agonist arrives, where there is no gating and the
variance is instrumental alone, while every other parameter has no information there at all.

THE DIGEST HAD TO GROW FOR IT. figure_3_digest.R kept param_index 0, 1, 2 and 5, the four identified
parameters; the noise is 3 and the baseline 4. Both are kept as of 2026-07-31, which cost one pass
over the seven ~1 GB dumps and about three and a half minutes, and makes the param table 600,000
rows instead of 400,000. The baseline is kept and drawn by nobody: no sentence in the paper is about
it.

ROSTER: all seven, widened from the body's four on 2026-07-31. The earlier note here said the other
three were supplement 1's business and that adding them would make a grid of near-null panels. The
INR run settled it the other way: row B is one of the checks INR passes and the recursive trio
fails, so the panels are not near-null and the contrast is the figure's content, not padding.

TWO-BLOCK Y SCALE ON ROWS B AND C, the parent's split (naive LSE/NR | recursive R/IR) on the rows
the parent splits. Row A is shared across all four on purpose: its claim is that nothing separates,
and a per-block scale would magnify noise into an apparent difference.

DATA: figures/data/digest/figure_3_digest_{LSE,NR,INR,R,MR,VR,IR}.rds. Cell N_ch = 100, Current_Noise = 1e-4,
interval = 0.1 tau, 1000 recordings, seed 20260722. B = 400 percentile bootstrap replicates over
recordings, the figure_3 family convention. Every number the caption quotes is printed by the
caption-numbers chunk on each knit.

SUPERSEDES the residual triptych built earlier the same day (mean, variance and autocorrelation of
the residual in three rows), which was three quarters contained in the parent: its variance row was
the parent's row B and its score-autocorrelation series the parent's row G. What was genuinely new
in it went two ways -- the residual autocorrelation into the parent's row G, where it sits beside
the score and their gap can be read off one panel, and the residual mean here. The superseded file
is kept at tmp/triptych_superseded.Rmd until the thread closes.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r read}
# ALL SEVEN, widened from the body's four on 2026-07-31 with supplement 2 and for the same reason:
# INR passes every per-interval check and fails only the accumulated one, and rows A and B here are
# two of those checks. On row B it reads 0.11, 0.10 and 0.01 across the three parameters against a
# chance level of 0.05, second only to IR and ahead of all three recursive members, which is the
# non-monotonicity along the cost ladder that MR and VR have to be present to show.
ALGOS <- c("LSE", "NR", "INR", "R", "MR", "VR", "IR")
LAB   <- c(LSE = "LSE", NR = "NR", INR = "INR", R = "R", MR = "MR", VR = "VR", IR = "IR")
FLAB  <- c(LSE = "Least\nSquares", NR = "Non-\nRecursive", INR = "Interval Non-\nRecursive",
           R = "Recursive", MR = "Mean\nRecursive", VR = "Variance\nRecursive",
           IR = "Interval\nRecursive")
LEAD  <- ALGOS[1]
B     <- 400
FMIN  <- 1e-6      # absolute information floor, as in the parent

# The three parameters the parent does not draw. param_index in the digest: 0 = k_on,
# 1 = k_off, 2 = unitary_current, 3 = Current_Noise, 4 = Baseline, 5 = Num_ch_mean. The parent has
# 1 and 5; 4 is kept in the digest and drawn by nobody.
PSEL <- c(k_on = 0L, i = 2L, noise = 3L)

dg <- setNames(lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  f <- sprintf("../data/digest/figure_3_digest_%s.rds", a)
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("missing digest for ", a, ": run figure_3_digest.R ", a)
  readRDS(f)
}), ALGOS)

SCAL <- rbindlist(lapply(ALGOS, function(a)
  as.data.table(dg[[a]]$scalar)[, .(key = a, simulation_index, sample_index, t, agonist, r_std)]))
PAR  <- rbindlist(lapply(ALGOS, function(a)
  as.data.table(dg[[a]]$param)[param_index %in% PSEL,
    .(key = a, simulation_index, sample_index, param_index, s, I)]))
if (!nrow(PAR)) stop("no rows for PSEL: the digests predate the six-parameter extraction, re-run ",
                     "figure_3_digest.R")
PAR[, param := factor(names(PSEL)[match(param_index, PSEL)], levels = names(PSEL))]
tmap   <- unique(SCAL[key == ALGOS[1], .(sample_index, t, agonist)])[order(sample_index)]
n_samp <- nrow(tmap)
setorder(SCAL, key, simulation_index, sample_index)
setorder(PAR,  key, param, simulation_index, sample_index)
```

```{r stats}
set.seed(20260731)
wide <- function(d, val) as.matrix(dcast(d, simulation_index ~ sample_index, value.var = val)[, -1])

# Row A: the mean standardized residual, bootstrapped over recordings like every band in the family.
bootmean <- function(d, val) {
  M <- wide(d, val); n <- nrow(M)
  rep <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) colMeans(M[sample.int(n, n, TRUE), , drop = FALSE],
                                                 na.rm = TRUE), numeric(ncol(M)))
  data.table(sample_index = as.integer(colnames(M)), m = colMeans(M, na.rm = TRUE),
             lo = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
             hi = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
RMEAN <- merge(SCAL[is.finite(r_std), bootmean(.SD, "r_std"), by = key], tmap, by = "sample_index")

# Row B: the standardized score bias, resampled as the WHOLE ratio so it carries the correlation
# between the score and its own information rather than treating Fbar as known. Same estimator as
# the parent's row D.
bias_stats <- function(d) {
  Sm <- wide(d, "s"); Im <- wide(d, "I")
  smp <- as.integer(colnames(Sm)); n <- nrow(Sm)
  Fb <- colMeans(Im)
  rep <- matrix(NA_real_, B, length(smp))
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    rep[b, ] <- colMeans(Sm[idx, , drop = FALSE]) / sqrt(colMeans(Im[idx, , drop = FALSE]))
  }
  data.table(sample_index = smp, Fbar = Fb, zA = colMeans(Sm) / sqrt(Fb),
             lo = apply(rep, 2, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
             hi = apply(rep, 2, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
BIAS <- merge(PAR[, bias_stats(.SD), by = .(key, param)], tmap, by = "sample_index")
dB   <- BIAS[is.finite(zA) & is.finite(Fbar) & Fbar > FMIN]

# Row C: the score autocorrelation, one per recording then a row-resample of the stacked matrix.
LAGMAX  <- min(25, n_samp - 2)
acf_one <- function(x) as.numeric(acf(x, lag.max = LAGMAX, plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass)$acf)
ACF <- PAR[, {
  M <- do.call(rbind, .SD[, .(a = list(acf_one(s))), by = simulation_index]$a)
  n <- nrow(M)
  rep <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) colMeans(M[sample.int(n, n, TRUE), , drop = FALSE]),
                numeric(ncol(M)))
  .(lag = 0:LAGMAX, acf = colMeans(M),
    lo = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi = apply(rep, 1, quantile, .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}, by = .(key, param)][lag >= 1]
```

```{r caption-numbers}
cat("\n=== Figure 3 supplement 2 caption numbers (n_simulations =",
    uniqueN(SCAL$simulation_index), "| members:", paste(ALGOS, collapse = ", "),
    "| parameters:", paste(names(PSEL), collapse = ", "), ") ===\n")
on  <- tmap[agonist > 0, sample_index]
pre <- tmap[sample_index < min(on), sample_index]

cat("\nA  mean standardized residual, whole record, and the fraction of steps whose 95% interval\n",
    "   excludes zero. The row's whole claim is that nothing separates:\n")
tabA <- merge(SCAL[is.finite(r_std), .(mean_r = mean(r_std)), by = key],
              RMEAN[, .(frac_steps_CI_excludes_0 = mean(lo > 0 | hi < 0)), by = key], by = "key")
print(as.data.frame(tabA[match(ALGOS, key)]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nB  score bias: fraction of informative steps whose 95% interval excludes zero",
    "(0.05 is the chance level):\n")
print(as.data.frame(dB[, .(f = mean(lo > 0 | hi < 0), n_steps = .N), by = .(key, param)][
      order(match(key, ALGOS), param)]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n   where each parameter is informative at all, as a step count out of", n_samp,
    ". The noise level is the only one\n   measured BEFORE the agonist arrives, where the variance",
    "is instrumental alone:\n")
INF <- BIAS[, .(steps_informative = sum(Fbar > FMIN),
                of_those_pre_agonist = sum(Fbar > FMIN & sample_index %in% pre)),
            by = .(key, param)][order(match(key, ALGOS), param)]
print(as.data.frame(INF), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nC  score autocorrelation at lag one:\n")
print(as.data.frame(ACF[lag == 1, .(key, param, acf1 = acf, lo, hi,
      resolved = lo > 0 | hi < 0)][order(match(key, ALGOS), param)]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n   the parent draws k_off and N_ch on this statistic, and its row G also carries the",
    "residual\n   autocorrelation: LSE 0.846, NR 0.510, R 0.118, IR -0.010.\n")
```

```{r panels, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 5.8}
# Colour. k_off's blue and N_ch's vermillion are spoken for by the parent and the neutral dark is
# the residual's, so the three parameters here take the remaining Okabe-Ito hues that survive the
# green null line. Under deuteranopia they read as light blue / reddish grey / orange, which
# separate on lightness as well as hue.
PCOL <- c(k_on = "#56B4E9", i = "#CC79A7", noise = "#E69F00")
PLEG <- c(k_on = expression(k["on"]), i = expression(italic(i)),
          noise = expression(sigma["noise"]))
NEU  <- "#1A1A1A"
NUL  <- "#009E73"
pscale <- list(scale_colour_manual(values = PCOL, labels = PLEG, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
               scale_fill_manual(values = PCOL, labels = PLEG, name = NULL, drop = FALSE),
               guides(fill = "none"))

base <- function() theme_bw(base_size = 9)
tr   <- range(tmap$t)
lr   <- range(c(1, ACF$lag))
agon <- tmap[agonist > 0]; x0 <- min(agon$t); x1 <- max(agon$t)
# -Inf/Inf and not the family's old +-1e10, which draws nothing on a linear axis with a window of
# order one. Every row here is linear, so all three would have come out unshaded.
mkshade <- function() annotate("rect", xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                               fill = "grey85", alpha = .5)
padr <- function(r, f = .06) r + c(-1, 1) * diff(r) * f

# The open-loop block gains INR: it carries no recursion, which is the property the split is about.
NAIVE  <- intersect(ALGOS, c("LSE", "NR", "INR", "NMR"))
blkof  <- function(a) if (a %in% NAIVE) "naive" else "rec"
KEYBLK <- setNames(vapply(ALGOS, blkof, ""), ALGOS)
AXIS_AT <- c(ALGOS[1], ALGOS[vapply(ALGOS, blkof, "") == "rec"][1])
qrng2 <- function(D, cols, p = c(.005, .995)) {
  lapply(split(names(KEYBLK), KEYBLK), function(ks) {
    v <- unlist(lapply(cols, function(k) D[key %in% ks][[k]]))
    as.numeric(quantile(v[is.finite(v)], p, na.rm = TRUE))
  })
}
rng2 <- function(D, cols, incl = NULL) {
  lapply(split(names(KEYBLK), KEYBLK), function(ks) {
    v <- unlist(lapply(cols, function(k) D[key %in% ks][[k]]))
    range(c(v[is.finite(v)], incl), finite = TRUE)
  })
}
pick <- function(yl, a) if (is.list(yl)) yl[[blkof(a)]] else yl

sym_breaks <- function(ylim) {
  s <- max(abs(ylim)); st <- c(.005, .01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .5, 1, 2)
  st <- st[st <= s]; if (!length(st)) return(0)
  k <- st[length(st)]
  sort(unique(c(-k, 0, k)[c(-k, 0, k) >= ylim[1] & c(-k, 0, k) <= ylim[2]]))
}
deco <- function(p, col, xr, ylim, yq, bottom = FALSE, xlab = NULL, split = FALSE) {
  p <- p + scale_y_continuous(breaks = sym_breaks(ylim)) + coord_cartesian(xlim = xr, ylim = ylim)
  shows <- split && col %in% AXIS_AT
  if (col == LEAD) p <- p + ylab(yq) + theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8))
  else if (shows) p <- p + theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
  else p <- p + theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                      axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  if (bottom) {
    if (col == ALGOS[2]) p <- p + xlab(xlab) + theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8))
    else p <- p + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
  } else p <- p + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
  p + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(0.5, 3, 0.5, 3))
}

colhead <- function(a) ggplot() + theme_void() +
  ggtitle(bquote(bold(.(LAB[[a]]))), subtitle = FLAB[[a]]) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5, size = 9, margin = margin(b = 0.5)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = .5, size = 7, margin = margin(b = 0)),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
rowlet <- function(lt) ggplot() + theme_void() +
  annotate("text", x = .5, y = .97, label = lt, size = 8 / .pt, fontface = "bold", vjust = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
rowstrip <- function(txt) ggplot() + theme_void() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = .15, xmax = 1, ymin = .03, ymax = .97, fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  annotate("text", x = .575, y = .5, label = txt, angle = -90, size = 6.5 / .pt, lineheight = .9) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
RTTL <- c(A = "residual\nmean", B = "score bias", C = "score\nautocorrelation")

# --- A: the mean residual. Parameter-free, so neutral, and on ONE scale across the four columns:
# the row's claim is that nothing separates, and a per-block scale would manufacture a difference
# out of noise.
yA <- padr(range(c(RMEAN$lo, RMEAN$hi), finite = TRUE))
pA <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(RMEAN[key == a], aes(t, m)) + mkshade() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = NEU, alpha = .22) +
    geom_line(colour = NEU, linewidth = .4) + base()
  deco(g, a, tr, yA, expression(bar(r)[t]))
})
# --- B: the score bias for the three parameters. Percentile limits, not extremes: the concentration
# jump would otherwise set the scale for the whole row.
yB <- lapply(qrng2(dB, c("lo", "hi")), padr, .08)
pB <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(dB[key == a], aes(t, zA, colour = param, fill = param)) + mkshade() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = .20, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .4, show.legend = FALSE) + base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, tr, pick(yB, a), expression(bar(s)[t] / sqrt(F[t])),
       bottom = TRUE, xlab = "time (ms)", split = TRUE)
})
# --- C: the score autocorrelation over lag, three series dodged so the intervals at one lag do not
# read as one bar.
yC <- lapply(rng2(ACF, c("lo", "hi"), incl = 0), padr, .08)
pC <- lapply(ALGOS, function(a) {
  g <- ggplot(ACF[key == a], aes(lag, acf, colour = param)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = NUL, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = .3, show.legend = FALSE,
                   position = position_dodge(width = .55)) +
    geom_point(size = .25, position = position_dodge(width = .55), show.legend = FALSE) +
    base() + pscale
  deco(g, a, lr, pick(yC, a), "ACF", bottom = TRUE, xlab = "lag", split = TRUE)
})

# Hand-drawn key under the grid, one clause per entry: it is laid out in panel fractions, so an
# over-long label does not wrap, it runs off the page. That happened once on supplement 1.
keyplot <- local({
  seg <- function(x, y, col) annotate("segment", x = x, xend = x + .035, y = y, yend = y,
                                      colour = col, linewidth = .6)
  txt <- function(x, y, lab) annotate("text", x = x + .046, y = y, hjust = 0, size = 6.5 / .pt,
                                      label = lab, parse = TRUE)
  xs  <- c(.015, .105, .195)
  lbs <- c('k["on"]', 'italic(i)', 'sigma["noise"]')
  g <- ggplot()
  for (j in seq_along(PSEL)) g <- g + seg(xs[j], .70, PCOL[[names(PSEL)[j]]]) + txt(xs[j], .70, lbs[j])
  g + annotate("text", x = .30, y = .70, hjust = 0, size = 6.5 / .pt,
               label = "score, rows B and C") +
    seg(.53, .70, NEU) +
    annotate("text", x = .576, y = .70, hjust = 0, size = 6.5 / .pt,
             label = "standardized residual, row A") +
    annotate("text", x = .015, y = .22, hjust = 0, size = 6.5 / .pt,
             label = paste("Bands and intervals are 95% nonparametric bootstrap over the 1,000",
                           "recordings. Grey marks the agonist pulse.")) +
    theme_void() + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), expand = FALSE) +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 0, 0, 0))
})

#        head    A     B     C
HS <- c(0.15,  0.85, 0.95, 0.90)
ROWS  <- list(A = pA, B = pB, C = pC)
STRIP <- TRUE
nc    <- length(ALGOS) + 2
cells <- unlist(lapply(names(ROWS), function(k)
  c(list(rowlet(k)), ROWS[[k]], if (STRIP) list(rowstrip(RTTL[[k]])))), recursive = FALSE)
grid <- wrap_plots(c(
    list(plot_spacer()), lapply(ALGOS, colhead), if (STRIP) list(plot_spacer()), cells),
  ncol = nc,
  widths = unit(c(0.112, rep(1, length(ALGOS)), if (STRIP) 0.203),
                c("in", rep("null", length(ALGOS)), if (STRIP) "in")),
  heights = HS)
g <- grid / keyplot + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.075))
# RENAMED and RESIZED 2026-08-05. Figure 3 now carries three supplements: the per-step information
# figure was split in two (Figure_3_S1 / Figure_3_S2) because at 7.0 x 11 in it could not fit a
# supplement page, and this one follows them as S3. Width 5.6 in, not 7.0: a figure supplement is
# placed in the 5.65 in text column, so 7.0 in art was arriving scaled by 0.81 with its text 19%
# under whatever size it was set at. Height scaled with the width to keep the panel shape.
ggsave("Figure_3_S3.pdf", g, width = 5.6, height = 4.64)
cat(sprintf("wrote Figure_3_supplement_2.pdf: 3 rows, %d members, %d parameters, 7.0 x 5.8 in\n",
            length(ALGOS), length(PSEL)))
```
